spells.json.note: Descriptions, material components and higher-level notes retranslated from the English SRD; names preserved via -preserve name. Reasoning effort is recorded because it changes the output: without it the model dropped the clauses naming other spells.

otherCollections.note: Prose not retranslated, but repaired: dice moved to Latin notation, metric conversions put back to imperial, and the numbers that had drifted from the English corrected by hand. magic-items.json, features.json, equipment.json and traits.json now pass the same prose checks as spells.json and are listed in proseChecked.

terminologyReferences.name: DnD.su 2014
terminologyReferences.usage: Entity titles only. Every spell name and every school name is matched to its DnD.su title; the seventeen spells whose names the SRD strips of their wizard (Melf, Bigby, ...) keep the de-named form. No descriptions or user comments copied. Damage type and condition names are matched to the same vocabulary: piercing and slashing had been swapped, and poisoned read as 'ядовитый', poisonous, which is the opposite sense.

terminologyReferences.name: Long Story Short SRD 5.1
terminologyReferences.usage: Terminology reference only. Its translations are author-owned -- the site permits personal non-commercial use and short quoted fragments, and forbids republishing complete materials or derivative works without written permission -- so no prose from it is used here. Its separate /srd/ project has no translated spells.

proseConventions.measurements: Imperial, with Russian unit words -- футов, фунтов, миль. Never metres or kilograms: the client renders the structured range as футов, so converted prose contradicted the facts panel of the same spell.
proseConventions.numbers: Every number and die in the English survives translation. Enforced by valuesMatch in cmd/llm/translate.go and by TestRussianProseKeepsEveryNumber. Compared as a set, not a tally, because 'N feet square' is idiomatically 'N на N футов' in Russian.
